summary: No Apurímac-specific trans statute, ordinance, enforcement finding or incident appears in the sources attached to this record. The department stands under the national framework of Peru, and the national assessment carried by the parent record applies to a trans visitor here.
tangentialFactors:
The three attached sources are national in scope. Infobae Perú (20 February 2025) reports a congressional Women and Family Commission action, IDEHPUCP (15 April 2025) analyses a plenary vote of the national Congress, and Agencia Presentes (22 July 2024) reproduces nationwide observatory figures. None records conduct, facilities or incidents in Apurímac, so none can be read as evidence about conditions in the department.

The violence statistics are national raw counts: 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases across Peru for 2020–2023, with trans women accounting for 30 of the homicides. The source gives no per-capita figures and no departmental breakdown, so these totals cannot be converted into a rate for Apurímac or used to rank it against other departments.
localsOnly: No resident-facing rule specific to Apurímac — a regional government directive, a municipal signage or facility practice, or a documented local enforcement pattern — is sourced in this record. What is documented for residents of the department is the national legislation described in the parent record, which applies uniformly and is not modified by any Apurímac instrument found here.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the national restroom restriction has been applied in practice in Abancay or other towns of the department is unresolved: no source attached to this record documents an enforcement encounter, an ID check or a complaint filed in Apurímac.

Local institutional posture is not sourced. Nothing here establishes how Apurímac's regional government, municipal authorities, health facilities or police respond to trans residents or visitors, and no regional hate-crime or violence data for the department was available to test against the national pattern.

The commission-stage and plenary actions described in the attached sources are national legislative steps; their implementation timeline and any constitutional challenge reaching Apurímac courts remain unresolved in these materials.
